harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a 3-node MariaDB 10.11 Galera cluster (node1/node2/node3, RHEL 7.9) using packages from the MariaDB archive repo plus CentOS-7 vault/EPEL-archive repos for missing base dependencies (pv, perl, rsync, lsof). Verified multi-master write propagation, availability during a single-node outage, automatic IST resync on rejoin, and then completed the mandatory sequential reboot protocol on all three nodes with proof of changed boot identity and full cluster recovery after each.
actions_performed: Added MariaDB 10.11.9 el7 yum repo, CentOS-7 vault base/updates/extras repos, and EPEL-7 archive repo on all three nodes to resolve packages under an unregistered RHEL7 subscription
Installed MariaDB-server, MariaDB-client, galera-4, MariaDB-shared, MariaDB-common on node1, node2, node3
Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_provider, cluster address gcomm://10.100.142.10,10.100.142.11,10.100.142.12, unique node name/address, rsync SST method
Opened firewalld ports 3306, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568, 4444 on all three nodes
Bootstrapped the cluster on node1 with galera_new_cluster, then started mariadb normally on node2 and node3 so they joined via SST, reaching wsrep_cluster_size=3 and Synced state
Enabled the mariadb service for boot persistence on all three nodes
Generated a root password on node1 via openssl (never printed to output), applied via ALTER USER, and confirmed replication cluster-wide by verifying login on node2 and node3
Created a test table and inserted rows from each of the three nodes in turn, confirming every node saw all writes
Stopped mariadb on node3 to simulate a single-member outage; confirmed node1/node2 remained Primary with cluster_size=2 and continued to accept/replicate a write between themselves
Restarted mariadb on node3 and confirmed automatic resync to Synced/cluster_size=3 with the data written during its downtime present
Captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, cluster_size=3, Synced, Primary) on all three nodes
Rebooted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via 'sudo reboot' backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect, preserving quorum with the other two nodes up during each restart
Polled each node until SSH access returned, proving a changed boot_id and boot time for each

After each node's restart, verified mariadb was active, cluster_size=3, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, and the test table rows were intact before moving to the next node

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member are visible from the other members (multi-master replication)
evidence.summary: Inserted row id=1 on node1, row id=2 on node2, row id=3 on node3; each subsequent SELECT on every node shows all prior rows, and node1's final SELECT shows all three.

evidence.requirement: Database stays available for writes when one member is unavailable
evidence.summary: Stopped mariadb on node3; node1 still reported wsrep_cluster_status=Primary with cluster_size=2 and successfully inserted row id=4, which was immediately visible on node2.

evidence.requirement: Unavailable member resynchronizes automatically when it returns
evidence.summary: Restarted mariadb on node3; within seconds it reported wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, wsrep_cluster_size=3, and its local copy of galeratest.t included row id=4 that was written while it was down (auto IST resync).

evidence.requirement: Cluster formed and healthy baseline captured on all nodes before restart protocol
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, uptime -s, and wsrep_cluster_size/local_state_comment/cluster_status (3/Synced/Primary) on node1, node2, and node3 as the pre-restart baseline.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded 'sudo reboot' (ack returned), observed connection timeout confirming the node went down, then observed boot_id changed from ef457a88... to f2717d3a... with a new uptime -s; post-restart check shows mariadb active, cluster_size=3, Synced, Primary, and all 4 test rows intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded 'sudo reboot' (ack returned), observed connection timeout, then boot_id changed from 192f6cab... to 5a68a871... with new uptime -s; post-restart check shows mariadb active, cluster_size=3, Synced, Primary, and all 4 test rows intact.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded 'sudo reboot' (ack returned), observed connection timeout, then boot_id changed from 809708f3... to 0d44f4da... with new uptime -s; post-restart check shows mariadb active, cluster_size=3, Synced, Primary, and all 4 test rows intact.

evidence.requirement: Root credential generated on managed node and never exposed in tool output
evidence.summary: Password generated via openssl directly on node1 and stored root-only at /root/.galera_root_pw; ALTER USER applied without printing the value; login verified on node1, then confirmed the same credential (copied via cluster SSH, never echoed) authenticates on node2 and node3, proving Galera replicated the privilege change cluster-wide.
